notes: The '1+ coins' phrasing put the Simulation stat-grinder family in play, and I checked it deliberately: that family's tell is tiers in a line with a wall between each pair that a number opens, plus upgrades and a rebirth pad, and none of it is here — there is no barrier the coins unlock, nothing to spend them on, and the intake answer says one full QWERTY board is the whole course. So the self-declared obby leads, the challenge stays geometric jumps between keys that must be physics-legal, and the genre-wide P6 is earned rather than imported; Simulation is named second because the coin-per-key accrual is a real earning loop. Shape is course-flat since a laptop keyboard is a single horizontal surface progressed across, so no tiered and no P2. Took Classic Obby and added station-training from the secondary genre, bent to mean every key on the board pays out when stepped on, which is what the prompt describes rather than collectible-nodes' coins placed on risky lines; without a user I assumed the run ends at the far edge of the board and gave it winner-zone, and kept the preset's checkpoints and obstacles as the standard obby vocabulary the thin prompt leaves open.
